The yaw sweep tested 120°–240° in 0.5° steps at a fixed 27.5° upward tilt. The candidate increases combined two-tag cases from 39/81 to 43/81 per alliance. Either yaw retains at least one tag in 80/81 cases; one perturbation near C loses both. It is a sampled visibility choice, not a verified physical optimum.

Position, angle and simulation details

Measured bumper length and width: 0.86995 m. The chassis frame is 0.7112 m square. Position A is bumper contact with the released hub face at X=12.512261 m; B is 0.86995 m farther toward the wall; C is bumper contact with the tower at X=15.434500 m. Y=4.034500 m and robot heading=180° for all red-side shots.

Camera lens approximation in robot WPILib coordinates: X=−0.324056 m, Y=+0.292100 m (left), Z=0.208004 m. The user’s left-side correction supersedes the side shown in the earlier snapshot study. Camera yaw is measured counterclockwise from robot-forward (+X), looking down from above. Yaw 180° is rearward; 191° aims 11° toward robot-right from rearward. Camera roll remains 180° (inverted). Official wall tags remain upright.

PhotonVision uses nominal 1280×800, 82°×56.2° optics, zero calibration noise, a 25-pixel minimum target area, and 12 m maximum range. Field rays use the registered released 2026 mesh, a current drivetrain snapshot with its camera translated to the left, and an earlier static shooter snapshot. Any of nine tag sample rays blocked excludes that tag. Wiring, flex, unmodeled mount geometry, mechanism sweep, lighting and motion blur are excluded.

Field source: AdvantageScope 2026 field assets. Field registration maximum tag residual: 0.966 mm. Positive tower-hit and negative outside-field control rays passed.
